fix_decisions.note: Critical. Criterion 20 requires empty and comment-only run_sql text to be refused with a client text beginning 'Refused by the rule set:'. In the shipped composition WholeRowSelectGuardRunner wraps RuleSetGuardRunner and refuses both cases first as UnsafeSqlError, which the redactor maps to REDACTED_PARSE. Fixing it means deciding which component owns the refusal text for unparseable input under a rule-set file - reorder the two guards, or widen the redactor's parse arm - and both change behaviour the issue does not settle plus ordering and text that existing tests and internal docs pin. Reached at the iteration cap with no review round left to check a fix.

Suggestion. WholeRowSelectGuardRunner's docstring omits RuleSetGuardRunner from the runners it wraps. Not fixed: iteration cap reached with a blocking Critical open; bundled into the handoff for the next round.
Inconclusive. Criterion 11's live-MySQL integration test cannot be settled by reading source and no MySQL server was available in this run.

phase3_findings.description: src/sqllens/server.py lines 206-209 say the declared-key count replaces the extras count; both bounds apply, and the corrected sibling prose in row-level-security.md line 281 now disagrees.

docs/external/rule-sets.md line 66 says confirmed_against_production = true is required, contradicting line 99: only the key is required, and a set carrying false loads with a warning and is refused at selection time.

Freshness markers on the internal pages this change edits predate the edits: rule-sets.md line 3 records 97783a1, two commits behind head, and read-only-safety.md, row-level-security.md, agent/factory.md, setup/preflight.md, setup/config-loading.md and mcp-server/tools.md keep older markers.

docs/internal/database-connectors/rule-sets.md line 64 says a refusal recognized by _logged_by_guard is redacted to REDACTED_GUARD_ERROR; redacted_refusal_text returns a statement-refusal kind for every RlsError before _logged_by_guard is consulted, so the RLS and relation paths report REDACTED_RLS and REDACTED_RELATION instead.

src/sqllens/rule_sets.py line 243 hard-codes connect_timeout=5, duplicating preflight._DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS on the request-time path where an unreachable database makes every refused request wait the full timeout inside the turn lock.

src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py lines 113-116: comment-only text parses to a single None element, so the guard takes the statements[0] is None branch but logs the detail 'expected one statement, got 1', a count that does not explain the refusal.

src/sqllens/agent/factory.py lines 70-84: _RuleSetUserResolver falls back to the shared DEFAULT_USER_ID with no log when no selection is published, while every other rule-set component treats a missing selection as an error.
src/sqllens/tools/query_database.py lines 229-245 probe conversation_store.owner_id with getattr plus a hand-raised TypeError in place of a method the ConversationStore protocol does not declare.

src/sqllens/rule_sets.py lines 174-178: TableRule.row_rule is an Any field used only for presence detection via model_fields_set, so an explicit row_rule=None is rejected and the type says nothing about a version-2 row rule.
